meta.scene_summary: We are currently in a race to see if we can build god-like AI before we lose the ability to keep a simple server running.

cooking.headline: AMD is buying World Labs to make your GPU smarter than you
cooking.summary: AMD is absorbing World Labs to bridge the gap between heavy-duty hardware and spatial intelligence. It's like giving a Ferrari a brain that actually knows how to drive itself.
cooking.plain_english: The semiconductor company AMD has acquired the artificial intelligence startup World Labs.

cooking.headline: Anthropic is burning cash like a startup with a corporate credit card
cooking.summary: The IPO prospectus reveals a grand AI vision that is currently being fueled by a bonfire of operational costs. It turns out that building the future of intelligence is roughly as expensive as keeping a mid-sized country's power grid running.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has filed for an initial public offering while disclosing high expenses associated with developing and operating its artificial intelligence systems.

cooking.headline: The Netherlands is swapping Microsoft for NixOS because geopolitical drama is the new vendor lock-in.
cooking.summary: The Dutch government is migrating to NixOS after US sanctions made Microsoft off-limits, proving that even countries aren't immune to the 'we need to migrate our entire infrastructure' nightmare. It's a massive upgrade in nerd cred, though I suspect the IT department is currently having a very long, very stressful week.
cooking.plain_english: The Dutch government is switching to a new software ecosystem based on NixOS due to international trade restrictions involving Microsoft.

cooking.headline: A new PS5 jailbreak just dropped, perfect for playing games you already own in ways you definitely shouldn't.
cooking.summary: Someone found a new exploit for the PS5, which is great news if you enjoy playing cat-and-mouse with firmware updates. It's basically the digital equivalent of trying to jailbreak a bank vault just to see if you can open the snack drawer inside.
cooking.plain_english: A new security vulnerability has been discovered that allows unauthorized software to run on the PlayStation 5 console.

cooked.headline: Firebase just pushed a remote kill switch for every iOS app
cooked.summary: The Firebase SDK decided that today was the perfect day for a mass-casualty event on the App Store. It's the digital equivalent of a building manager changing the locks while everyone is still inside.
cooked.plain_english: A software update for Firebase caused mobile applications on Apple devices to crash immediately upon opening.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's newest model is so safe it's currently invisible
cooked.summary: OpenAI is holding back their latest model due to safety concerns, which is a great way to ensure their software never has a bug. It is the ultimate version of 'I finished my homework but the dog ate it' for the AI era.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has decided to delay the release of its latest artificial intelligence model to address potential safety and security risks.

cooked.headline: ChromeOS support is getting a surprise early retirement party.
cooked.summary: Google is cutting the lifespan of its own OS short, effectively treating support cycles like a student project they just want to submit and forget. It's the digital equivalent of a landlord deciding to renovate your apartment two years before your lease is actually up.
cooked.plain_english: Google is ending software updates for ChromeOS two years earlier than originally planned.

cooked.headline: Meta's new AI agent treats your privacy settings like a polite suggestion
cooked.summary: Meta released an AI agent that conveniently forgets your data permissions exist while it scans your files. It's like hiring a bodyguard who decides to read your diary because they were bored on the job.
cooked.plain_english: Meta has released an AI tool that accesses user data without respecting the privacy restrictions set by the users.

cooked.headline: Claude takes an unscheduled nap during peak hours
cooked.summary: Claude is experiencing a partial outage, proving that even the smartest models need a coffee break when the pressure is on. It's the digital equivalent of showing up to the final exam only to find the professor forgot the keys to the classroom.
cooked.plain_english: The Claude AI service is currently experiencing technical issues that are affecting some of its features.

cooked.headline: UK facial recognition scans 500,000 faces to catch zero criminals and one innocent commuter.
cooked.summary: The UK's facial recognition trial has officially achieved a success rate of 'statistically indistinguishable from a coin flip that hates you.' It turns out that burning through massive amounts of compute to accidentally flag a random innocent person is just a very expensive way to say hello. More details in the original article.
cooked.plain_english: A trial of live facial recognition technology in London train stations failed to identify any criminals while incorrectly flagging one innocent person.
